I couldn't do this research. The search and fetch tools hit a usage limit and timed out after only one search worked, so I read just part of one page. I can't give you notes on the rest of the chapter, and I won't fill the gaps from memory.

**What I found (all from one source)**

Source: Enduring Word, David Guzik, Ezekiel 18 (I only saw the summary and "High Points" at the top of the page): https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-18/

- **vv. 1–3:** Guzik treats the sour-grapes proverb as false and popular. It said the present generation was being punished unfairly for their fathers' sins. He says God corrects this hopeless, fatalistic way of thinking. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-18/
- **v. 4:** For Guzik this verse is God's answer to the proverb, built on two statements: every soul belongs to God, and the soul who sins will die. He takes this to mean God judges each person on their own, not families or communities as a group. He calls the idea "revolutionary" for Ezekiel's first hearers. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-18/
- **vv. 5–20:** He reads the three cases (a righteous man, his wicked son, and that son's righteous son) as showing that being righteous or wicked is not passed down from parents. Each person is judged by their own choices. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-18/
- **vv. 21–28:** His summary stresses that anyone can always turn from their sins. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-18/
- **vv. 30–32:** He calls this the chapter's summary and call to action. He sees the command to make "a new heart and a new spirit" as pointing ahead to the new covenant. The part I saw cut off mid-sentence, so I can't say how he develops that. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-18/

**Still to research**

1. **Verse-by-verse traditional reading:** the full Enduring Word page, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com or studylight.org, and preceptaustin.org.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ.** These verses look most likely to show differences, but I haven't checked any of them:
   - v. 24, whether a righteous person can turn away and be lost: Reformed teachers (ligonier.org, monergism.com) against Wesleyan ones (wesley.nnu.edu, seedbed.com).
   - vv. 23 and 32, God taking no pleasure in death, and how that fits with election: desiringgod.org against Wesleyan sources.
   - v. 31, "make yourselves a new heart" set beside God's promise in 36:26 to give one (free will against grace).
   - v. 20 and the doctrine of original sin.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes, bibleodyssey.org, Catholic and Orthodox sources on vv. 20 and 31, and any popular modern teaching about inherited curses or "generational curses" that uses vv. 2–4.

If you ask again later, I can run these searches one at a time to stay under the limit and fill in the notes.
